questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. The teacher, ___ I respect a lot, retires next month.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the object of 'respect' and refers to a person, so 'whom' is used.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. The tree has lost all ___ leaves.
questions.explanation: The possessive of a singular thing is 'its'. 'It's' always means 'it is' or 'it has'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. It is I who ___ responsible.
questions.explanation: A relative pronoun 'who' takes the person of its antecedent. Here the antecedent is 'I' (first person), so the verb is 'am'.
questions.shortcut: who takes the person of its antecedent.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. We should respect ___ elders.
questions.explanation: A possessive determiner is needed before the noun 'elders'. The subject is 'we', so 'our'.
questions.shortcut: Possessive before a noun: my, our, your, their.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. The principal gave the trophy to ___ had scored the highest.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the subject of 'had scored', so the subject form 'whoever' is used, even after 'to'.
questions.shortcut: The pronoun's role inside its own clause decides the case.

questions.questionText:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence. A. You and him are invited.
B. You and he are invited.
C. Him and you are invited.
D. You and himself are invited.

options.text: B. You and he are invited.
C. Him and you are invited.
D. You and himself are invited.
A. You and him are invited.

questions.explanation: The pronouns are the subject of 'are', so the subject form 'he' is needed. 'Him' is the object form, and 'himself' is reflexive.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. The Smiths have sold ___ house.
questions.explanation: 'The Smiths' is plural, so the possessive is 'their'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. Ramesh, along with his friends, has lost ___ way.
questions.explanation: 'Along with' does not change the subject, which is 'Ramesh' (singular masculine). So 'his'.
questions.shortcut: Pronoun agrees with the main subject.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. I do not know ___ has taken my pen.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the subject of 'has taken', so the subject form 'who' is used.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. All the guests except Sheela and ___ had left.
questions.explanation: 'Except' is a preposition, so it takes the object form 'me'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. He is the man ___ I believe is guilty.
questions.explanation: 'I believe' is a parenthetical clause. 'Who' is the subject of 'is guilty', so the subject form is needed.
questions.shortcut: Drop 'I believe' and test: '___ is guilty'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. The reward will go to ___ the committee thinks is most deserving.
questions.explanation: Inside its clause, the pronoun is the subject of 'is most deserving' ('the committee thinks' is parenthetical), so 'whoever'.
questions.shortcut: Drop the parenthetical clause and test the case.

questions.questionText:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence. A. Neither of the sisters wanted to share their room.
B. Neither of the sisters wanted to share her room.
C. Neither of the sisters wanted to share its room.
D. Neither of the sisters wanted to share our room.

options.text: C. Neither of the sisters wanted to share its room.
B. Neither of the sisters wanted to share her room.
D. Neither of the sisters wanted to share our room.
A. Neither of the sisters wanted to share their room.

questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular, so the pronoun that refers to it must be singular and feminine: 'her'. 'Their' is plural, 'its' is for things, and 'our' changes the speaker.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. Those of ___ who attended the camp were awarded certificates.
questions.explanation: 'Of' is a preposition, so the object form 'us' follows it.

questions.questionText:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence. A. The Government has announced its decision, and they will implement it soon.
B. The Government has announced its decision, and it will implement it soon.
C. The Government have announced its decision, and they will implement it soon.
D. The Government has announced their decision, and it will implement it soon.

options.text: D. The Government has announced their decision, and it will implement it soon.
A. The Government has announced its decision, and they will implement it soon.
C. The Government have announced its decision, and they will implement it soon.
B. The Government has announced its decision, and it will implement it soon.

questions.explanation: A collective noun acting as a single body takes singular pronouns throughout. B is consistent: 'has', 'its', 'it'. The others shift between singular and plural.
questions.shortcut: Keep one number for the same noun.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. The chief guest, ___ speech inspired everyone, left early.
questions.explanation: The word shows possession (the guest's speech), so 'whose' is needed.

questions.questionText:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence. A. It is me who is responsible.
B. It is I who is responsible.
C. It is I who am responsible.
D. It is me who am responsible.

options.text: A. It is me who is responsible.
D. It is me who am responsible.
C. It is I who am responsible.
B. It is I who is responsible.

questions.explanation: After 'it is', the formal complement is the subject form 'I'. The relative 'who' takes the person of 'I', so the verb is 'am'.

questions.questionText: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence. The people ___ I work with are friendly.
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the object of the preposition 'with' and refers to people, so 'whom' is used.
